messages:
Maya R: Heads up — incident page for the 11:12 GFP inference spike is closed. Impacted ~3 customers for ~22m, root cause was an autoscale misconfig + cache eviction window. oncall-bot created a draft postmortem and 3 actions. Who can take the follow-up scheduling?

Sam P: I can book it. Can we get the postmortem into the standard template before the meeting? Last time the notes were all over the place.

oncall-bot: Incident 1919000000 resolved. Postmortem draft created: /pm-drafts/1919000000. Actions: A1 (assign), A2 (investigate autoscale policy), A3 (improve runbook).

Maya R: Thanks. @Sam P, please host. @Lina (SRE) can you lead technical RCA? Alex, can you pull customer-impact chat logs so we can quantify downtime per tenant?

Lina (SRE): Happy to lead RCA. Quick ask: the draft's action items are free-text — can we get them into the action dashboard automatically? We keep losing owners during handoffs.

Alex G: I'll pull the customer logs and Uptime metrics. For automation: ops-runbook-bot has an API to create tasks in the tracker, we could call it in the postmortem template generator.

Sam P: Proposed meeting window: Thursday 10–11am PT. I'm adding a calendar invite now. Agenda: timeline, RCA, customer impact, action assignment, owners + due dates.

Maya R: Good. Lina — can you add short pre-reads to the draft (timeline + key logs) so folks can skim? Also we should include a snippet with the autoscaler config that caused the gap.

Lina (SRE): Yep. Minimal pre-read will include: timeline, `kubectl describe hpa inference-pool`, `redis-cli info` output for the cache eviction spike, and sampling of failed requests.

Alex G: Uploading customer impact table to the draft. We'll include per-tenant token loss and estimated revenue exposure.

Maya R: On tooling improvements I want to discuss two quick automation ideas during meeting: 1) postmortem template plug-in that emits structured action items (owner, due, severity) and POSTs to our action-dashboard API; 2) improved handoff ephemeral checklist emitted at oncall transition with outstanding PM actions flagged.

Sam P: +1. For (1) we need a stable JSON schema. Current templates are markdown blobs. If ops-runbook-bot accepted a payload like:

```
{
  "incident": "1919000000",
  "summary": "GFP inference autoscale gap",
  "actions": [
    {"title": "Tighten autoscale policy range", "owner": "Lina (SRE)", "due": "2024-06-28"},
    {"title": "Cache eviction monitoring", "owner": "Alex G", "due": "2024-06-25"}
  ]
}
```

then it could create atomic tasks in the dashboard.

ops-runbook-bot: Ops-runbook-bot can accept /create_tasks payloads. Current endpoint: `POST https://ops.example/api/tasks` with bearer token. Rate limit small (5/s).

Lina (SRE): That looks reasonable. Also want a guard: if the template includes an action without an owner, bot should prompt for assignment, not create unowned items.

Maya R: Agreed. Also propose we add a tiny step in the oncall handoff script that lists "open PM actions > 48h" and pins them to the next standup. That would reduce action leakage.

Alex G: Implementation quick sketch: we can add a cron job that queries actions with status!=done && created_at < now()-48h and posts summary to #oncall-daily and adds them to the handoff ephemeral message.

Sam P: Can we get a demo of the automation in the meeting? If Lina or Alex can show the bot creating tasks from the draft JSON it will speed adoption.

Maya R: Yes, schedule the demo. Lina, Alex — pair for a 20 min run-through before Thursday so we can surface blockers.

Lina (SRE): I'll prototype a small script that translates the markdown template to the JSON schema. Sharing snippet now:

```
python md_to_actions.py --input postmortem.md --output postmortem.json
# then
curl -X POST https://ops.example/api/tasks -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOT_TOKEN" -d @postmortem.json
```

Sam P: Nice. A couple process asks to add to the agenda: enforce that postmortems include a customer-impact section (per-tenant), and require owners + due dates for all actions before closing the meeting.

Maya R: Agreed. Also add a tiny SLA: if an action is high-priority (sev >= P1), owner must ack within 24h or it escalates to SRE lead. We'll add that to the template schema as `priority` and leverage ops-runbook-bot for escalations.

ops-runbook-bot: Acknowledged. Can attach `priority` field and create an `on_ack` webhook to notify SRE leads.

Alex G: One more thing — the handoff notes should include the list of customers with degraded experience and recommended comms. We should template the customer-impact blurb so Support can copy/paste.

Maya R: Good point. I'll add a short copy template to the postmortem template: subject, short summary, recommended mitigation text, and how to reach oncall.

Sam P: All set on my side. I'll post invite and link to draft. Meeting on Thursday 10am PT, 60 mins.

Maya R: Thanks everyone. Action owner recap (quick):
- Lina: RCA doc + pre-reads + prototype md->json (due Tue)
- Alex: Customer-impact table + demo data pull (due Wed)
- Sam: Meeting + agenda + invite + ensure demo slot (done)
- Maya: Add comms template + SLA escalation clause in schema (due Wed)

Lina (SRE): I'll ping here once md->json prototype is up.

Alex G: Demo data ready — will share sample payload in thread before meeting.

Maya R: closing loop — oncall-bot, can you mark postmortem draft with status=ready_for_review when pre-reads attached?

oncall-bot: Updated postmortem 1919000000 status -> ready_for_review (pre-reads: timeline.md, logs.zip, customer-impact.csv).

Maya R: :thumbsup: See you all Thursday.
